result.title: PIA: Agentic Physics-Informed Runtime Anomaly Detection
result.summary: Runtime anomaly detectors for cyber-physical systems are either learned as black boxes from normal data, which miss stealthy manipulations that keep every signal inside its normal range, or derived by hand from physical models, which requires expert effort for every plant. We introduce physicsinformed agents (PIA), in which a large language model agent writes the detector itself as a set of physical residuals, such as pump characteristics, tank mass balances, and controller logic, and refines every candidate against normal operating data through an evaluation workbench before deployment. The result is a compact, human-readable detector that runs in milliseconds and names the component behind each alarm. On the BATADAL water distribution attack benchmark, PIA with Claude Opus 5.5 reaches an F1 of 0.878 on the test attacks against 0.504 for the strongest of six statistical and deep baselines, keeps detecting attacks concealed by replayed and offset sensor readings, and attributes every detected test attack to the attacked component. Ablations show that testing hypotheses against data is decisive: agents that write residuals from the plant description alone lose up to 0.28 F1, whereas agents that see only anonymized signals recover most of the physical structure.

AI.brief_summary: PIA 让 LLM agent 依据物理模型自行编写由泵特性、质量平衡、控制器逻辑等物理残差组成的运行时异常检测器，并在部署前用正常工况数据在评估工作台上筛选候选；在 BATADAL 攻击基准上 F1 明显优于统计与深度基线，并能给出被攻击组件的归因。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「生成候选假设—用数据检验—淘汰仅凭先验写出的残差」闭环，与 LVR 中 latent 是否真正依赖视觉证据、以及如何筛选与停止的评估问题可能形成类比，可供核查数据接地检验的设计思路。
